learning_objective: The learner will use the contrast ratio and the 4.5 and 3 minimums to decide whether each of nine color pairs passes for normal text, passes for large text only, or fails, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** contrast-ratio-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** use
**Learning Objective:** The learner will use the contrast ratio and the 4.5 and 3 minimums to decide whether each of nine color pairs passes for normal text, passes for large text only, or fails, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Color Contrast, Contrast Ratio, Color Independence (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each pair the learner commits one of three verdicts after seeing the colors and before the ratio is shown. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content. Mastery is at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. Using the explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) If two colors look different, they pass. (2) Rounding 4.499 up to 4.5 makes it pass. (3) Large text needs the same ratio as normal text. **Instructional Rationale:** Using a numeric threshold on measured values is an Apply-level action. Predicting from sight first, and then seeing the measured ratio, shows the learner that sight is unreliable near the threshold, which is the reason the check exists. **Content:** The thresholds, shown at all times: normal text needs a ratio >= 4.5; large text (18 points or larger, or 14 points or larger if bold) needs a ratio >= 3.0. The three verdicts: Passes for normal text (ratio >= 4.5), Passes for large text only (ratio >= 3.0 and < 4.5), Fails (ratio < 3.0). The nine pairs, with each ratio computed from relative luminance as the chapter states: | # | Text color | Background color | Ratio | Correct verdict | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | #000000 | #FFFFFF | 21.00 | Passes for normal text | The largest possible ratio. | | 2 | #757575 | #FFFFFF | 4.61 | Passes for normal text | The ratio is at least 4.5. | | 3 | #949494 | #FFFFFF | 3.03 | Passes for large text only | The ratio is at least 3.0 and less than 4.5. | | 4 | #FFFFFF | #1A5FB4 | 6.29 | Passes for normal text | White text on a deep blue has a high ratio. | | 5 | #FFFFFF | #FF8C00 | 2.33 | Fails | White on orange is less than 3.0, so no text size passes. | | 6 | #FF0000 | #FFFFFF | 4.00 | Passes for large text only | Red on white is at least 3.0 and less than 4.5. | | 7 | #767676 | #F0F0F0 | 3.99 | Passes for large text only | The same gray that passes on white is less than 4.5 on a light gray background. | | 8 | #DDDDDD | #FFFFFF | 1.36 | Fails | Pale gray on white has almost no contrast. | | 9 | #FFFFFF | #2E7D32 | 5.13 | Passes for normal text | White on a dark green has a ratio of at least 4.5. | **Provenance:** The ratios are computed from the WCAG definition of relative luminance and are shown to two decimals. The color pairs are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The thresholds follow the chapter section "Contrast Ratio". **Rules:** The ratio is (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) with L1 the luminance of the lighter color and L2 that of the darker. Tests use the unrounded ratio. Each pair has exactly one correct verdict. In explore mode the learner enters a text color and a background color as hex codes, and the sim shows the ratio to two decimals and the three verdicts for normal text, for large text, and for graphics. Four pairs are Passes for normal text, three are Passes for large text only, and two are Fails. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner enters two colors and reads the ratio and the verdicts. 2. In practice mode the sim shows pair 1 as a sample of text on its background, without the ratio. 3. The learner chooses a verdict, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows the ratio, whether the verdict was correct, and the Why text. 5. After pair 9 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 9 pairs in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. The ratio is [ratio]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The ratio is [ratio], so this is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 9 correct on the first attempt". At 8 or more it adds "You can read a contrast ratio." Below 8 it lists the Why text of each missed pair. **Starting State:** Explore mode with black text on a white background and a ratio of 21.00. The prompt is "Enter two colors to see the ratio." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says normal text needs a ratio of at least 4.5 to 1, large text at least 3 to 1, black on white is 21 to 1, #767676 on white is 4.54 to 1, and #777777 on white is 4.48 to 1.
